fields.Name: Isolation Forest
fields.Description: Unsupervised anomaly detection by random isolation: an ensemble of trees with random feature + random threshold splits on small subsamples. Anomalies are 'few and different', so they separate in FEWER splits — the anomaly score is the normalized average path length to isolation. No labels, no density model, near-linear cost.

fields.Name: Dummy Classifier
fields.Description: The leaderboard FLOOR for classification: predicts from the class marginals of y alone (most-frequent / prior / stratified / uniform / constant) and never reads a single feature. Its entire purpose is to define the score any real model must beat — a candidate that cannot clear this floor has learned nothing from the features.

fields.Name: Dummy Regressor
fields.Description: The leaderboard FLOOR for regression: predicts a single constant — the training mean, median, a quantile, or a supplied value — for every row, never reading a feature. Under strategy='mean' it is the R²=0 line by definition: any real regressor must clear it to have learned anything from the features.

fields.Name: Gaussian Process
fields.Description: Bayesian nonparametric kernel model: a Gaussian prior over functions, conditioned exactly on the data. Its defining virtue is NATIVE uncertainty — every regression prediction is a full posterior N(μ,σ²), with σ honestly inflating away from the data. Its defining gate is cost: exact inference inverts the n×n kernel matrix, O(n³) time / O(n²) memory, ceiling ≈ 10k rows.

fields.Name: k-Nearest Neighbors
fields.Description: Instance-based lazy learner: prediction is a (distance-weighted) vote or mean over the k closest training rows. There is no real fit — training memorizes the data and builds a spatial index; ALL modeling effort happens at query time in the distance metric.

fields.Name: Multi-Layer Perceptron
fields.Description: Fully-connected feed-forward neural network trained by backprop (Adam/SGD/L-BFGS). A universal approximator whose capacity is set by hidden_layer_sizes; on typical business-tabular data it needs careful scaling, enough rows to feed its weight count, and usually fights gradient-boosting for the same slot rather than beating it.

fields.Name: Naive Bayes
fields.Description: Closed-form Bayes classifier under the strong assumption that features are conditionally INDEPENDENT given the class. Fits in one pass (per-class moments or counts), works at tiny n, ranks well — and is famously miscalibrated when features correlate, because shared evidence gets multiplied in as if it were new.

fields.Name: Support Vector Machine
fields.Description: Max-margin kernel machine: solves a dual QP to find the separating surface (or ε-tube, SVR) defined by a subset of support vectors, with the RBF kernel lifting the boundary to be nonlinear. Strong on small-to-medium clean numeric data; fit cost over the n×n kernel matrix is its ceiling.

fields.Name: DBSCAN
fields.Description: Density-based clusterer: grows clusters from core points (≥ min_samples neighbors within eps), discovering arbitrarily-shaped clusters WITHOUT choosing k, and labeling sparse points as noise (-1). Its defining operational edge: sklearn's DBSCAN has NO predict() for new points — assignment of unseen rows is a wrapper responsibility, which is exactly what makes it a wrapper-needs case study for the family.

fields.Name: Gaussian Mixture Model
fields.Description: Probabilistic clusterer: fits a weighted mixture of k Gaussians by EM. Its distinguishing emission is the SOFT assignment — per-row membership probabilities (responsibilities) rather than a hard label — and, because it is a genuine density model, it scores unseen points natively and doubles as an anomaly screen. The price is the elliptical assumption: every cluster is a mean + covariance ellipsoid.

fields.Name: Agglomerative (Hierarchical) Clustering
fields.Description: Bottom-up hierarchical clusterer: starts with every row as its own cluster and greedily merges the closest pair under a linkage criterion (ward/complete/average/single), producing a full merge tree — the dendrogram — that can be cut at ANY height, so the segment count is a post-fit choice rather than a pre-fit commitment. Like DBSCAN it has no native predict() for unseen rows (fit_predict only) — new-point assignment is a wrapper responsibility. interpretabilityClass 'Rules' is the nearest 4-way fit for the dendrogram: a human-readable nested merge structure, though not literal decision rules.

fields.Name: K-Means
fields.Description: Prototype-based partitioner; the clustering default. Alternates assign-to-nearest-centroid / recompute-centroid steps to minimize within-cluster squared Euclidean distance, yielding k compact spherical segments plus a readable k×p centroid matrix. k is selected by a silhouette sweep, not fixed a priori. Segmentation deliverable first, supervised feature second — see additionalObservations for the demand-gate lesson.

fields.Name: BG/NBD (Beta-Geometric / Negative Binomial)
fields.Description: Latent-attrition purchase model for non-contractual settings: Poisson purchasing while alive with Gamma-distributed rates across customers, and Beta-Geometric dropout that can occur only after a purchase. From an RFM summary alone it answers 'is this customer still alive?' (P(alive)) and 'how many purchases in the next t periods?' — without churn ever being observed.

fields.Name: Gamma-Gamma Monetary Model
fields.Description: The monetary companion to the transaction BTYD models: a customer's average transaction value is Gamma-distributed around a latent mean that is itself Gamma-distributed across customers. Produces the conditional expected average profit per transaction (empirical-Bayes shrinkage of the customer's observed average toward the population), and — composed with a fitted BG/NBD or Pareto/NBD — discounted customer lifetime value.

fields.Name: Pareto/NBD
fields.Description: The original (1987 Schmittlein-Morrison-Colombo) buy-till-you-die model and BG/NBD's continuous-time sibling: Poisson purchasing while alive with Gamma heterogeneity, and exponentially distributed customer lifetimes with Gamma heterogeneity (Pareto-II dropout). Dropout can occur at any instant — so P(alive) is an exact continuous-time posterior, well-defined and informative even for zero-repeat customers.

fields.Name: PCA
fields.Description: Linear dimensionality reduction via SVD of the (centered) data matrix: finds the orthogonal directions of maximum variance and projects rows onto the top k. Captures second-order (linear/covariance) structure only; the fitted linear map is reusable on new rows and the loadings are directly inspectable.

fields.Name: UMAP
fields.Description: Nonlinear manifold learning: builds a fuzzy k-NN topology of the data and optimizes a low-dimensional layout that preserves LOCAL neighborhood structure. Unrolls curved structure PCA cannot; the price is stochastic fits, unreliable global distances, and no meaningful inverse back to feature space.

fields.Name: ARIMA
fields.Description: Autoregressive integrated moving-average forecaster for a single time-indexed series; models autocorrelation and (with seasonal terms) periodicity, producing horizon forecasts with prediction intervals.

fields.Name: Croston (Intermittent Demand)
fields.Description: The intermittent-demand specialist: runs two separate exponential smoothers — one on non-zero demand SIZES, one on the INTERVALS between demand events — and forecasts the flat demand rate size/interval. Its niche is sparse series full of zeros (event registrations, per-chapter merch orders, low-volume renewals) where every mainstream forecaster smears the zeros into nonsense.

fields.Name: Exponential Smoothing (ETS)
fields.Description: Innovations state-space exponential smoothing: recursively weighted level, trend, and seasonal components with exponentially decaying memory. The workhorse mid-tier forecaster — more robust than ARIMA on short business series, strictly stronger than the naive floors when trend or seasonality is real.

fields.Name: Prophet
fields.Description: Decomposable curve-fit forecaster: piecewise-linear (or logistic) trend with automatic changepoints + Fourier-series seasonalities + holiday effects, fit as a regression on time via Stan MAP. Regression-on-timestamps rather than lag-recursion — which is why it tolerates gaps and irregular sampling that break ARIMA/ETS.

fields.Name: Seasonal Naive
fields.Description: The family FLOOR: forecast every future period as the value from the same position in the last observed seasonal cycle. Zero parameters, zero fit. It exists to be beaten — MASE is defined against it, so it IS the denominator of the family's honest scoreboard.

fields.Name: Simple Moving Average
fields.Description: Mean of the last k observations, held flat over the horizon. The family's second floor and its resident SMOOTHER: as a forecaster it is the level-only reference for non-seasonal series; as a preprocessor it emits the rolling-mean series itself for a downstream forecaster to consume.

fields.Name: Theta Model
fields.Description: Competition-proven simple forecaster (won M3, strong in M4): deseasonalize, then combine a linear-drift theta-line with an SES theta-line — equivalent to SES with drift on the deseasonalized series, reseasonalized. Near-zero tuning surface with accuracy that embarrasses far heavier methods on monthly/quarterly business series.

fields.Name: Generalized Additive Model
fields.Description: A GLM whose linear terms are replaced by penalized SMOOTHS: y's link-mean = intercept + f1(x1) + ... + fp(xp), each f a spline whose wiggliness is penalty-controlled. Keeps the GLM's per-feature interpretability (each effect is a plottable 1-D curve) while capturing nonlinearity a straight coefficient cannot — the midpoint between GLM and black-box.

fields.Name: Negative Binomial Regression
fields.Description: Count regression for OVERDISPERSED data: a Poisson mean with a gamma-mixed rate, adding an estimated dispersion parameter alpha so variance = mean + alpha*mean^2 (NB2). The honest upgrade from Poisson when variance outruns the mean — same log-linear coefficients, correctly-sized standard errors.

fields.Name: Ordinal Regression (Ordered Model)
fields.Description: Regression for ORDERED categories (satisfaction tiers, membership levels, risk grades): a single latent index x'B is cut by K-1 estimated thresholds into K ordered classes. One slope vector shared across all cutpoints (proportional odds) — the order in the target is used, not discarded as flat multiclass would.

fields.Name: Poisson GLM
fields.Description: The canonical count regression: models a non-negative integer target as Poisson-distributed with log-linear mean exp(x'B). Coefficients exponentiate to rate ratios; supports offsets/exposure for per-unit-time rates. Its defining commitment is equidispersion — variance EQUALS the mean.

fields.Name: Quantile Regression
fields.Description: Linear regression of a conditional QUANTILE instead of the mean: minimizes the asymmetric pinball (check) loss, so q=0.5 is median regression and tail q's map the outcome's spread. Makes NO distributional assumption on the errors — the family's distribution-free member, robust to outliers and heteroscedasticity.

fields.Name: Tweedie GLM
fields.Description: GLM for zero-inflated CONTINUOUS targets: with variance power p in (1,2) the Tweedie family is a compound Poisson-gamma — an exact point mass at zero plus a right-skewed positive tail — modeled in ONE equation. The canonical shape of insurance pure premium, per-member revenue, and claim/donation totals.

fields.Name: Zero-Inflated Count Model
fields.Description: Two-part count mixture: a logit/probit INFLATION submodel decides whether a row is a structural zero (never-participant), and a Poisson/NB COUNT submodel generates counts (including sampling zeros) otherwise. Separates 'won't ever' from 'didn't this time' — two coefficient stories one plain count model conflates.

fields.Name: CatBoost
fields.Description: Gradient-boosted ensemble of symmetric (oblivious) trees with ordered target statistics + optional ordered boosting (CPU default is Plain) and ordered target statistics — its distinguishing mechanism: raw categorical features are encoded internally without target leakage, so it is the strongest default on categorical-heavy tabular data.

fields.Name: LightGBM
fields.Description: Histogram-based gradient-boosted tree ensemble with leaf-wise (best-first) growth. Bins features into discrete histograms and grows the highest-gain leaf next, making it the fastest strong tabular learner at scale — with native missing-value and native categorical handling.

fields.Name: XGBoost
fields.Description: Gradient-boosted decision-tree ensemble; the strong tabular default. Additively fits shallow trees to the gradient of the loss, capturing non-linearities and interactions with minimal preprocessing.

fields.Name: Elastic Net
fields.Description: Convex blend of L1 and L2 penalties: keeps lasso's exact-zero selection while the L2 component adds the grouping effect — correlated features enter and leave the support TOGETHER instead of lasso's arbitrary single pick. The default when you want sparsity on correlated tabular data.

fields.Name: Lasso
fields.Description: L1-penalized least squares: the soft-thresholding geometry of the L1 ball zeroes coefficients exactly, so the fitted model IS a feature selection — the surviving support is the effect story. Fit by cyclic coordinate descent.

fields.Name: Logistic Regression
fields.Description: L2-regularized (by default) linear classifier: models the log-odds as a linear function of features and optimizes penalized log-loss. The transparent classification baseline — every coefficient is a per-unit log-odds effect — and natively near-calibrated because it trains on the proper scoring rule.

fields.Name: Multinomial Logit (statsmodels)
fields.Description: Unpenalized maximum-likelihood softmax classifier over K unordered categories, fit by Newton's method: (K-1) coefficient equations against a reference category, each with standard errors, z-tests, and confidence intervals. The multiclass inference sibling of ols — choose it to EXPLAIN category choice; choose sklearn's logistic_regression to predict it.

fields.Name: OLS (statsmodels)
fields.Description: Unpenalized least squares fit with the FULL inference apparatus: coefficients with standard errors, t-statistics, p-values, confidence intervals, and prediction intervals. This is the family's answer-the-why member — where sklearn's linear models predict, OLS testifies. Requires n > p and honest attention to its error assumptions.

fields.Name: Ridge Regression
fields.Description: L2-penalized least squares: shrinks all coefficients toward zero without zeroing any, trading a little bias for a large variance reduction. THE collinearity fixer — the penalty makes X'X + alpha*I invertible, so the solution stays unique and stable where OLS becomes ill-posed (including p > n).

fields.Name: Association Rules
fields.Description: Frequent-itemset mining plus rule induction over transaction baskets: finds itemsets whose co-occurrence support clears a floor, then derives antecedent->consequent rules scored by support, confidence, and lift. Emits a per-model RULES table; there is deliberately NO per-row scoring operation.

fields.Name: LDA Topic Model
fields.Description: Generative probabilistic topic model over count data: documents are mixtures of K latent topics, topics are distributions over the vocabulary, with Dirichlet priors on both simplices and a multinomial word likelihood fit by variational Bayes. Emits a per-row topic mixture. (Latent Dirichlet allocation — NOT LinearDiscriminantAnalysis, which shares the acronym.)

fields.Name: Implicit ALS
fields.Description: Alternating-least-squares matrix factorization for IMPLICIT feedback (clicks, plays, purchases — not ratings). Factorizes the user-item interaction matrix into low-rank user and item latent-factor matrices under the Hu-Koren-Volinsky confidence weighting, where unobserved cells are weak negatives, then ranks items per user by latent-factor dot product.

fields.Name: Rubric (Weighted Scorecard)
fields.Description: Glass-box linear scorer: operator-defined factors, each passed through a declared normalizer (percentile/minmax/zscore/logistic/banded/lookup, with a HigherIsBetter direction), combined by hand-set OR fitted weights into a single score, optionally banded into tiers. Every prediction decomposes EXACTLY into per-factor contributions — the weights are the whole story.

fields.Name: Hidden Markov Model
fields.Description: Latent-regime model over sequences: hidden states follow a Markov chain, each state emits observations from a parametric distribution (Gaussian or categorical). EM (Baum-Welch) fits states + transitions jointly; the validated Predictive Studio use is member activity-cadence regime as a downstream feature via the latent-state adapter.

fields.Name: Kalman Filter / Dynamic Linear Model
fields.Description: General linear-Gaussian state-space model: latent continuous states evolve linearly with Gaussian noise and are observed through a linear-Gaussian measurement. Exact filtering (real-time state estimate), smoothing (retrospective), and forecasting — with exact, in-model handling of missing observations. Local-level and local-linear-trend DLMs and time-varying-coefficient regression are canonical instances.

fields.Name: Discrete Markov Chain
fields.Description: First-order Markov chain over OBSERVED discrete states: estimates the K x K transition-probability matrix by counting state-to-state transitions across sequences. The matrix IS the model — fully inspectable, fit by counting, no latent structure.

fields.Name: Markov Switching Regression
fields.Description: Regime-switching model over a time series: a hidden first-order Markov chain selects which of k regimes' regression/AR parameters (and optionally variance) generates each observation. The product is the smoothed regime-probability path plus per-regime coefficients — 'which era is this series in, and how do its dynamics differ'.

fields.Name: Structural Time Series (Unobserved Components)
fields.Description: Decomposes a series into named latent states — level, trend, seasonal, cycle, AR — each an explicit stochastic component in one linear-Gaussian state space. The product is the interpretable decomposition itself (each state is a nameable curve), fitted by Kalman filtering/smoothing with exact missing-data handling.

fields.Name: Vector Autoregression
fields.Description: Multivariate linear dynamics over K aligned series: each series is regressed on p lags of ALL series, capturing cross-series lead-lag interdependence (Granger structure, impulse responses). The observed K-vector IS the state; the lag-coefficient matrices are its linear transition law — the fully-observed continuous analog of this family, as the Markov chain is its discrete one.

fields.Name: AFT (Log-Normal / Log-Logistic)
fields.Description: The generic parametric AFT alternatives to Weibull, covered by ONE driver with a `distribution` hyperparameter. Covariates rescale survival TIME (time-ratio reading, like weibull_aft) but the assumed lifetime distribution admits NON-monotone hazards — the hump-shaped/unimodal hazards Weibull cannot express. Neither distribution satisfies proportional hazards (log-logistic satisfies proportional ODDS instead), so this is the AFT-only branch of the family.

fields.Name: Cox Proportional Hazards
fields.Description: Semiparametric survival model: estimates per-feature hazard ratios against an unspecified baseline hazard, handling right-censored time-to-event data natively. Answers WHEN (and relative risk), not just IF.

fields.Name: Kaplan-Meier Estimator
fields.Description: Nonparametric POPULATION survival curve — the survival floor. Covariate-free: consumes only the (duration, event) pair, no feature matrix at all. Every covariate survival model (Cox, AFT, RSF) is compared against this baseline; if a model cannot beat the KM curve's summary, its covariates are earning nothing.

fields.Name: Random Survival Forest
fields.Description: Nonparametric ensemble survival model: bagged trees split by the log-rank statistic, with per-leaf Nelson-Aalen estimators aggregated into per-row survival curves. Captures nonlinearities and interactions no (semi)parametric survival model can, at the cost of coefficient-level interpretability (importances only) and a larger data appetite.

fields.Name: Weibull AFT
fields.Description: Fully parametric accelerated-failure-time model: covariates multiplicatively rescale survival TIME (exp(coef) is a time ratio — 'members with X last 1.3x longer'), vs Cox's hazard-ratio reading. Buys extrapolation beyond the observed window and absolute time predictions by assuming Weibull-distributed lifetimes.

fields.Name: Decision Tree
fields.Description: A single CART tree: recursive axis-aligned partitioning by impurity-minimizing threshold splits. The glass-box of the family — every prediction is a readable root-to-leaf rule path — at the cost of high variance that the ensemble siblings exist to average away. The value proposition is the explanation, not the accuracy ceiling.

fields.Name: Extra Trees
fields.Description: Extremely randomized tree ensemble: like a random forest but split thresholds are drawn at RANDOM within each candidate feature's range instead of optimized, and by default each tree sees the full sample (no bootstrap). Trades a little bias for a further variance drop and a much cheaper fit — the smoothing sibling of the forest.

fields.Name: Random Forest
fields.Description: Bagged decision-tree ensemble: each tree is fit on a bootstrap resample with a random feature subset per split, and predictions are averaged. Variance reduction by averaging — not additive error correction like boosting — makes it a robust, low-tuning tabular baseline that rarely embarrasses itself.

fields.Name: Isotonic Calibrator
fields.Description: Monotone probability recalibration. Fit on rows the base model never fit on (CV form preferred).

fields.Name: Platt Calibrator
fields.Description: Sigmoid probability recalibration; safe at low event counts.

fields.Name: Calibrator Template
fields.Description: Calibrator(model __): wraps any probability-emitting model with post-hoc calibration.

fields.Name: model
fields.Description: The probability-emitting model to calibrate

fields.Name: Cluster-then-Classify
fields.Description: Composes a clusterer's segment feature into a downstream classifier (via the cluster-id adapter).

fields.Name: cluster
fields.Description: The clustering component whose segment id feeds the classifier

fields.Name: classifier
fields.Description: The downstream probability-emitting classifier
